editorial:
Imagine a guy who is great at fighting but has no direction in life. That is Joe Armstrong. He is a drifter who loves martial arts but gets into trouble with the law. Instead of going to jail, he joins the Army and ends up in the Philippines. The movie feels like a classic throwback to the eighties, with a lot of energy and some really cool fight scenes. You get to see a reluctant soldier turn into a hero after a rebel group attacks his convoy and kidnaps the colonel's daughter. It is a straightforward story that does not try to be too deep, focusing instead on the thrill of the mission.

You will love the fast-paced action and the way the fight choreography looks for its time. While some of the acting is a bit cheesy and the plot is predictable, that is part of the charm. It is perfect for a lazy weekend when you just want to see some bad guys get beat up. If you want the best experience, you should look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, or you can just rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. It is a great pick if you miss those old-school action flicks.
endingExplained: After a long trek through the jungle, Joe tracks down the rebel base to save the colonel's daughter. He uses his ninja skills to sneak past guards and take out the enemy soldiers one by one. In the final showdown, Joe fights the lead villain in a high-stakes battle. Joe wins the fight, saves the girl, and stops the rebels from getting more weapons. He goes from being a troublemaker to a respected hero in the eyes of the Army.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s action movies and martial arts.
